panels.title: Exporter reaches SQL Server
panels.description: sql_exporter's own up: 1 when it could log in and run its collectors.

panels.title: SQL Server CPU
panels.description: CPU used by SQL Server over the last minute (mssql_cpu_percent).

panels.title: Blocked requests
panels.description: Requests waiting on another session's lock right now.

panels.title: Deadlocks
panels.description: Deadlocks in the dashboard's time range.

panels.title: User errors
panels.description: Errors returned to clients in the time range: failed statements, constraint violations, deadlock victims.

panels.title: Page life expectancy
panels.description: Seconds a data page stays in memory. Falling fast, or low for the server's memory, means memory pressure.

panels.title: Batch requests / s
panels.description: Batches received per second: overall throughput.

panels.title: Requests by state
panels.description: Executing user requests: running on a CPU, runnable (waiting for one), suspended (waiting on a lock, I/O or memory).

panels.title: Connections by database
panels.description: Open sessions per database.

panels.title: Blocking
panels.description: Requests blocked right now, and how long the longest of them has waited.

panels.title: Longest running request
panels.description: Elapsed time of the longest user request executing at each scrape.

panels.title: Blocking chains
panels.description: From the collector's query samples (db.server.query_sample): every request seen blocked, the session blocking it, what it waited on, and its statement.

panels.title: Deadlock graphs
panels.description: Every deadlock, from SQL Server's system_health session (db.server.deadlock). Expand one: the processes, the statements they ran, the resources they held and wanted, and which was chosen as the victim.

panels.title: Statements and procedures in the time range
Top statements
panels.description: mssql_query_stats over the time range: the 20 statements with the most elapsed time. Avg is per execution. Statements whose plan left the cache drop out.

panels.title: Top stored procedures
panels.description: mssql_procedure_stats over the time range: the 20 procedures with the most elapsed time.

panels.title: Top waits
panels.description: What requests waited on most in the time range (mssql_wait_stats, idle waits left out). LCK_*: blocking; PAGEIOLATCH_*: reading pages from disk; WRITELOG: log writes; SOS_SCHEDULER_YIELD / CXPACKET: CPU and parallelism.

panels.title: Queries with more than one plan
panels.description: mssql_query_store: queries Query Store has seen run with several plans, and how much slower their slowest plan is than their fastest. A big ratio is a plan regression: force the fast plan with EXEC sp_query_store_force_plan @query_id, @plan_id (the plan ids are in the next table).

targets.expr: max by (database, query_id, query) (mssql_query_store_plan_avg_duration_seconds) / min by (database, query_id, query) (mssql_query_store_plan_avg_duration_seconds)

panels.title: Their plans
panels.description: Each plan of those queries: how often it ran and its average duration. Forced shows a plan pinned with sp_query_store_force_plan.

panels.title: Plan warnings
panels.description: The plans of the top queries (db.server.query_plan), with what usually makes a plan slow pulled out of the XML: an implicit conversion that blocks a seek, a key lookup per row, a scan, a spill to tempdb, a missing index, a join with no predicate. Cost is the optimizer's estimate.

panels.title: Execution plans
panels.description: The plan XML itself (db.server.query_plan): match it to the table above by sqlserver_query_hash in the line's details. Save one as .sqlplan to open it graphically in SSMS or Azure Data Studio.

panels.title: Procedure definitions
panels.description: The source of the procedures in the top list (db.server.procedure_definition).

panels.title: Missing-index suggestions
panels.description: mssql_missing_indexes: indexes the optimizer wanted, top 10 per database by estimated improvement. Overlapping suggestions are common: combine them, and weigh the write cost, before creating any.

panels.title: Unused indexes
panels.description: mssql_index_usage: indexes every write maintains but no query has read since SQL Server started. Candidates to drop, once the uptime covers a full business cycle.

panels.title: Database size
panels.description: Data and log file sizes per database, and how much of the log is in use. A log that stays full is waiting on a log backup (full recovery) or a long transaction.

panels.title: I/O latency
panels.description: Average time per read and per write, per database and file type (mssql_io_files): stall divided by count. Log writes above a few ms slow every commit.

panels.title: tempdb
panels.description: tempdb space by use: temp tables (user objects), sorts and hashes (internal objects), row versions (version store).

panels.title: Last backup
panels.description: Time since each database's last backup of each type finished. Never backed up shows as never.

panels.title: Log growths
panels.description: Times a transaction log had to grow in the time range: each growth stalls writes; size the log so it doesn't have to.

panels.title: Agent running
panels.description: Whether SQL Server Agent is running: if it isn't, no job runs, and nothing says so.

panels.title: Failing jobs
panels.description: Enabled jobs whose last run failed.

targets.expr: count(mssql_agent_job_last_outcome == 0 and on(job_name) mssql_agent_job_enabled == 1) or vector(0)

panels.title: Jobs
panels.description: mssql_agent: every job, its last outcome, how long ago its last run started and how long it took, and the failed runs still in its history.

panels.title: SQL Server error log (Linux compose stack)
Failed logins
panels.description: "Login failed" entries in the error log in the time range: a wrong password, a missing login, or someone guessing.

panels.title: Error log
panels.description: SQL Server's own error log (event db.server.errorlog), read from the container's log directory: startup, recovery, failed logins, I/O and memory errors. Not collected from the Windows runs.
